# =============================================================================
# The common parameter set ("management genome"). Every WET2024 type is ONE row
# = one point in this space. Nothing is a discrete category in the code; the WET
# codes are just names for parameter combinations. Per-species parameters
# (Zielstaerke, Mischungsregulierung) are shown for the LEADING species; the real
# WET specifies them per admixed species (see limitations).
#
# Parameter ranges / meaning:
#   zielstaerke_cm          target_diameter_cm       (Zielstaerke)            cm
#   nutzungsstaerke         target_harvest_fraction  (Nutzungsstaerke)        0..1 of >=target stems removed per entry
#   streubreite_cm          target_diameter_spread   (Zielstaerken-Streubreite) cm, sharpness of the target threshold
#   durchf_staerke          thinning_intensity       (Durchforstungsstaerke)  0..1 of basal area per entry (sub-target)
#   durchf_art              thinning_size_bias       (Durchforstungsart)      -1 Nieder .. 0 neutral .. +1 Hochdurchforstung
#   mischungsreg            species_removal_pref     (Mischungsregulierung)   0 keep leading .. 1 convert away from it
#   verjuengung             planting_rate            (Verjuengung / Vorbau)   0 natural regen .. 1 active planting
#   turnus_a                entry_interval_years     (Eingriffsturnus)        years between interventions
#   risikostufe             risk_level               (Risikostufe)            0 gering .. ~0.4 mittel .. ~0.8 hoch
# =============================================================================

wet <- data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  code  = c("b","bx","e","h","j","p","f","fx","m","t","tx","d","k","kx"),
  name  = c("Buchen-Mischwald","Buchen-Mischwald (hohes Risiko)","Eichen-Mischwald",
            "Buntlaubbaum-Mischwald frisch","Buntlaubbaum-Mischwald trocken","Pappel-Mischwald",
            "Fichten-Mischwald","Fichten-Mischwald (hohes Risiko)","Fichten-Kiefern-Moorwald",
            "Tannen-Mischwald","Tannen-Mischwald (hohes Risiko)","Douglasien-Mischwald",
            "Kiefern-Mischwald","Kiefern-Mischwald (hohes Risiko)"),
  lead  = c("Bu","Bu","Ei","Es/BAh","Es/BAh","Pa","Fi","Fi","Fi/Kie","Ta","Ta","Dgl","Kie","Kie"),
  zielstaerke_cm  = c(60,50,70,50,50,60,50,45,NA,55,50,65,50,45),
  nutzungsstaerke = c(0.5,0.7,0.4,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.6,0.8,0.0,0.5,0.7,0.5,0.5,0.7),
  streubreite_cm  = c(15,10,15,10,10,8,8,5,NA,12,8,15,10,8),
  durchf_staerke  = c(0.15,0.15,0.20,0.20,0.15,0.20,0.20,0.20,0.0,0.15,0.15,0.25,0.20,0.20),
  durchf_art      = c(0.3,0.2,0.4,0.4,0.3,0.3,0.2,0.0,0.0,0.2,0.1,0.5,0.3,0.2),
  mischungsreg    = c(0.15,0.35,0.20,0.20,0.25,0.10,0.15,0.40,0.0,0.15,0.35,0.15,0.20,0.40),
  verjuengung     = c(0.0,0.2,0.3,0.2,0.2,0.6,0.1,0.3,0.0,0.0,0.2,0.3,0.3,0.3),
  turnus_a        = c(7,5,7,7,7,5,7,5,NA,7,5,7,7,5),

    "Hohe Risikostufe: verkuerzte Zieldurchmesserernte, kein flaechiger Schirm; Umbau zu trockentoleranteren Begleitern.",

    "Sammeltyp vieler Edellaubbaeume mit sehr unterschiedlichen Zielstaerken (40-60 cm); ein Zielstaerkenwert ist grob.",

    "Zielstaerkennutzung/Dauerwald ersetzt den frueheren Kahlschlag-Umtrieb; klassische Niederdurchforstung nur naeherungsweise als leichte Auslese.",
    "Kernfall Klimaanpassung: Zielstaerke gesenkt (45 cm), schnellere Ernte, aktiver Umbau.",

    "Schattbaumart, Naturverjuengung; Zielstaerke gestaffelt (B 50 / geaestet bis 80 cm).",
    "Hohe Risikostufe der Tanne: verkuerzte Erntephase, Beimischung sichern.",
    "Anbaubaumart, oft gepflanzt; ausgepraegte Z-Baum-orientierte Hochdurchforstung. Zielstaerke stark qualitaets-/aestungsabhaengig (50-80 cm).",

# The common parameter set

Each WET2024 type is represented by the **same** parameters --- it is a *point in
this space*, never a hard-coded case. The operator turns them into a per-cohort,
per-entry **removal fraction**

\[
\begin{aligned}
r(\text{dbh}, s) = \mathrm{clamp}\Big(\;
& \underbrace{\text{nutzungsstaerke}\cdot\sigma\!\big((\text{dbh}-\text{zielstaerke}_s)/\text{streubreite}\big)}_{\text{Zielstaerkennutzung}} \\
&{}+ \underbrace{\text{durchf\_staerke}\cdot g(\text{dbh};\text{durchf\_art})\cdot f(\text{mischungsreg}_s)}_{\text{Durchforstung}}
\;,\,0,\,1\Big)
\end{aligned}
\]

applied on entry years (spacing `turnus_a`), while `verjuengung` acts on the
regeneration side (bringing target species *in*). `risikostufe` is a single dial
that lowers `zielstaerke` and shifts the tending --- it reproduces the WET risk
levels continuously.

| code parameter | WET-Begriff (deutsch) | Bedeutung | Bereich |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target_diameter_cm` | **Zielstärke** (Zieldurchmesser) | DBH at which a tree is harvested | cm |
| `target_harvest_fraction` | **Nutzungsstärke** | share of $\ge$ target stems taken per entry | 0–1 |
| `target_diameter_spread` | **Zielstärken-Streubreite** | sharp vs. gradual target threshold | cm |
| `thinning_intensity` | **Durchforstungsstärke** | basal-area share removed per entry (sub-target) | 0–1 |
| `thinning_size_bias` | **Durchforstungsart** | $-1$ Niederdurchf. … $+1$ Hochdurchf. | $[-1,1]$ |
| `species_removal_pref` | **Mischungsregulierung / Baumartenwahl** | keep leading (0) … convert away (1) | 0–1 |
| `planting_rate` | **Verjüngung / Vorbau** | natural regen (0) … active planting (1) | 0–1 |
| `entry_interval_years` | **Eingriffsturnus** | years between interventions | a |
| `risk_level` | **Risikostufe** | gering (0) … mittel (~0.4) … hoch (~0.8) | 0–1 |

## Limitations shared by all types

- **Per-species parameters shown for the leading species only.** A real WET sets
  `Zielstärke` and `Mischungsregulierung` per admixed species; the full vector is
  the intended representation, the table shows the lead value.
- **Z-Baum selection is approximated by a size bias.** WET tending is a
  crop-tree-*targeted* Auslesedurchforstung around marked Z-Bäume;
  `thinning_size_bias` reproduces its size signature, not the individual/spatial
  selection.
- **Structural/retention rules are outside the demography** (Habitatbäume, Totholz,
  Rückegassen, site and soil constraints, protected biotopes).
- **Risk maps are an external input.** `risk_level` sets the strategy dial; which
  stand sits at which risk level comes from the WET risk maps, not from FINN.

# The WET2024 types

Each type below is a **worked example**: the *same* illustrative stand (a single,
fast-growing species — hand-set, not fitted) run under that WET's management
parameters, so the figure isolates what the treatment does. The orange line is the
stand under the WET; grey is the same stand left unmanaged. Species-composition
effects (different Leitbaumarten, Mischungsregulierung) are not shown by a
single-species stand — they are documented in the table above. The point of these
examples is that FINN turns the parameter table into stand development you can *see*
and compare — a way to learn what each WET's programme actually does.

```{r sections, results = "asis"}
ex <- read.csv("examples/summary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(wet))) {
  w <- wet[i, ]; e <- ex[ex$code == w$code, ]
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s (`%s`)\n\n", w$name, w$code))
  cat(sprintf("*Leitbaumart:* %s  \n", w$lead))
  cat(sprintf("*Parameter:* Zielstärke %s cm | Nutzungsstärke %s | Streubreite %s cm | Durchforstungsstärke %s | Durchforstungsart %s | Mischungsregulierung %s | Verjüngung %s | Turnus %s a | Risikostufe %s\n\n",
              w$zielstaerke_cm, w$nutzungsstaerke, w$streubreite_cm, w$durchf_staerke,
              w$durchf_art, w$mischungsreg, w$verjuengung, w$turnus_a, w$risikostufe))
  cat(sprintf("![](examples/%s.png){width=70%%}\n\n", w$code))
  if (e$entries > 0)
    cat(sprintf("**Beispiel.** Held near **%.0f m2/ha** (unmanaged ~34) via %d entries; removed trees average **%.0f cm** BHD -- %s.\n\n",
                e$residual_ba, e$entries, e$mean_Dg_aus,
                if (isTRUE(w$risikostufe >= 0.7)) "the lower Zielstaerke and shorter Turnus of the high-risk variant take more, smaller stems" else "a graduated thinning working toward the target diameter"))
  else
    cat("**Beispiel.** No regular utilisation (Prozessschutz); the stand follows the unmanaged trajectory.\n\n")
  cat("**Grenzen der Abbildung.** ", w$comment, "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```
